introduction.title: Introduction to Sous Vide
introduction.whatIsBody: Sous vide is a method of cooking in vacuum sealed plastic pouches at precisely controlled temperatures. This allows for consistent results, enhanced flavor retention, and the ability to cook tough cuts of meat to a tender texture without overcooking.
introduction.stage1Body: Seasoning can be tricky. Use the [brine|Brine & Marinade Ratio Tool] to calculate the precise salt and sugar amounts for optimal moisture retention. Avoid raw garlic (use powdered) and extra virgin olive oil for long cooks.
introduction.stage2Body: Cooking is done in a water bath. Use the [doneness|Doneness & Texture Visualizer] to choose your target temperature. Use the [heating|Heating Time Calculator] to ensure the food reaches that temperature. For safety, especially with long cooks or vulnerable populations, use the [pasteurization|Pasteurization Calculator].
introduction.stage3Body: Since sous vide food looks poached when removed from the bag, it is usually finished by searing. Use a very hot pan with smoking oil or a blowtorch to create a flavorful crust (Maillard reaction) without overcooking the interior.
introduction.stage4Body: If not serving immediately, rapid cooling is essential to prevent spore outgrowth. Use the [chilling|Rapid Chilling Calculator] to determine ice-bath times. Use the [shelf-life|Shelf-Life & Storage Timer] to know how long your pasteurized food stays safe in the fridge.
introduction.safetyNoteBody: Food safety in sous vide depends on both temperature and time. This application uses the mathematical models from [https://douglasbaldwin.com/sous-vide.html|Dr. Douglas Baldwin] to calculate the minimum times required to reduce pathogens to safe levels.

heating.title: Heating Time Calculator
heating.explanation: Estimates how long it takes for the center of your food to reach the water bath temperature. Useful for ensuring food is heated through without necessarily pasteurizing it.
heating.resultSuffix: to reach 0.5°C (1°F) less than bath temp

pasteurization.title: Pasteurization Calculator
pasteurization.explanation: Calculates the minimum time required to reduce pathogens (Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli) to safe levels based on protein type, thickness, and temperature.
pasteurization.safetyDesc: Double pasteurization time if using an acidic marinade.
pasteurization.errorTemp: Temperature out of range for this protein.

rapidChilling.title: Rapid Chilling (Cook-Chill) Calculator
rapidChilling.explanation: Determines the required time to chill sealed food in an ice bath to 5°C (41°F). Crucial for preventing spore outgrowth when storing food for later use.
rapidChilling.resultSuffix: in ice water (at least half ice) to reach 5°C (41°F)

brine.title: Brine & Marinade Ratio Tool
brine.explanation: Calculates the exact amounts of salt and sugar needed for optimal brining, improving texture and moisture retention for specific protein types.

doneness.title: Doneness & Texture Visualizer
doneness.explanation: Visualizes how temperature affects the texture and doneness of meat and fish, helping you choose the perfect target temperature.

rare.name: Rare
rare.desc: Cool red center. Soft and spongy texture.

medium_rare.name: Medium-Rare
medium_rare.desc: Warm red center. Firmer texture, more savory.

medium.name: Medium
medium.desc: Pink center. Firm texture, significant juice loss starts.

medium_rare.name: Medium-Rare
medium_rare.desc: Starting to flake, still very moist.

shelfLife.title: Shelf-Life & Storage Timer
shelfLife.explanation: Calculates the maximum safe refrigerator storage time for pasteurized, rapidly chilled food based on storage temperature. Alternatively, food can be frozen for up to a year.
shelfLife.error: Temperature is too high for safe extended storage.
